rationale: Clinical and functional evidence confirms that while neuroimaging in Popov-Chang syndrome (caused by pathogenic YWHAZ variants) frequently shows normal gross brain structure, structural brain anomalies (such as cerebellar hypoplasia, cerebral atrophy, and morphological defects) occur in a subset of affected patients. Therefore, the presence of structural neuroanatomical abnormalities cannot be used as an exclusionary criterion for Popov-Chang syndrome.

evidence.text: Brain imaging in Popov-Chang syndrome often shows normal morphology, but abnormal findings including nonspecific cerebellar hypoplasia and cerebral atrophy have been documented in affected individuals.

new_directions.question_text: What is the systematic prevalence of structural brain malformations across all molecularly confirmed YWHAZ/Popov-Chang syndrome patients when evaluated by standardized volumetric high-resolution 3T MRI?
new_directions.rationale: Initial cohorts reported that brain imaging tended to be normal with occasional findings of cerebral atrophy or cerebellar hypoplasia. Systematically applying standardized neuroimaging protocols to larger international cohorts will delineate the exact spectrum and frequency of midline and cortical anomalies.

new_directions.question_text: Do dominant-negative or loss-of-function missense variants in specific functional domains of YWHAZ correlate with higher penetrance of structural neurodevelopmental defects compared to haploinsufficiency/truncating variants?
new_directions.rationale: Differences between familial missense variants exhibiting structural abnormalities in animal models and de novo truncating alleles could explain why structural brain findings are observed only in a distinct subset of patients.
